get.description: Returns the per-sender allowlist for one messaging channel. `:channel` is one of `imessage`, `whatsapp`, `slack`, `discord`, `telegram`, `teams`, `googlechat`, `signal`. When `mode` is `off`, every inbound message passes through. When `mode` is `on`, only messages whose sender matches an entry in `senders` are forwarded to the AI — matching is tolerant (normalizes phone formatting, strips `@` prefixes, lowercases usernames). Data lives in `.vodou/channels/<channel>-allowlist.json` and is watched live; edits take effect without restart. Unknown channels return 404.

post.description: Flip between `off` (allow every sender) and `on` (only senders in the list). Writes to `.vodou/channels/<channel>-allowlist.json` and triggers a live reload in the running channel.

post.summary: Add an allowed sender to a channel
post.description:
Add a sender ID (phone, email, JID, Slack user ID, Discord snowflake, Telegram chat ID, or `@username`) to the channel's allowlist. Idempotent — re-adding an existing ID is a no-op. Optional `name` is shown in the UI.

**Per-channel gotchas — what to actually add (not what you might think):**
- **iMessage:** the contact's phone or email (iMessage stores phones as `+15551234567`; digits-only also matches).
- **WhatsApp:** the contact's phone with country code, or a group JID. *Don't* add the phone your Vodou bridge is paired with — that's the recipient account, not a sender.
- **Slack:** the channel ID (`C01…` public, `D01…` DM, `G01…` private) where conversations happen, AND the bot user ID so `@mention` events route through, AND any plain user ID (`U01…`) of a human you want to allow. In practice you need both a channel entry and the bot user entry.
- **Discord:** the human sender's user ID / `@username`, or a channel ID. *Don't* add your bot's own snowflake.
- **Telegram:** YOUR chat ID or `@username` — NOT the bot's. The bot is the recipient; the allowlist is the list of humans who can message it. Quickest way to find your chat ID: set `mode=off`, send the bot one message, grep `channels-telegram.log` for the logged ID.

post.summary: Remove an allowed sender from a channel
post.description: Exact-match removal by `id` (case-sensitive, same string you added with). If the sender isn't on the list, still returns `ok: true` with the current count.

get.summary: iMessage-only: top-N recent senders from chat.db
get.description: One-click import helper for the iMessage allowlist. Reads `~/Library/Messages/chat.db` (requires Full Disk Access granted to the Node process) and returns the most-frequent senders over the last ~6 months, sorted by message count. UI shows these as checkboxes in the 'Import top senders from Messages' modal. Optional `?limit=N` (1–100, default 20). Returns 400 on non-macOS and 404 if chat.db is missing.

Non-prompting probe of whether the Node interpreter running this gateway has Full Disk Access for `~/Library/Messages/chat.db`. Reads the first byte of the file — if TCC denies, returns `fullDiskAccess: 'missing'`; if granted, `'granted'`. Also reports `nodeBinaryPath` so the UI can tell the user exactly which binary to add in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Full Disk Access. Automation (Messages) permission can't be probed without prompting, so it always reports `'unknown'`.

grantTargets.why: Gateway + iMessage channel both run under this Node interpreter — it opens chat.db
